newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Rebels fire on Nigerian troops in S.Leone -witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Rebels fire on Nigerian troops in S.Leone -witnesses.

text.p: A unit of Nigerian troops in Sierra Leone came under fire from rebels on Sunday in the first attack on a regional force gearing up to end a week-long coup in Freetown, members of the unit said.

No one was injured in the attack on the highway into the capital from Hastings airport on the eastern outskirts of town. The four Nigerian soldiers said they did not return fire but the car in which they were travelling was riddled with bullet holes and managed to get to town with two tyres shot up.

"The rebels were chasing our car from a pickup van. They continued firing even after we entered the city. There was panic in the streets, I'll be surpised if no one was hit," one of the soldiers told Reuters.

Tension rose sharply in the capital on Sunday despite intensified diplomatic efforts to persuade coup leader Major Johnny Paul Koromah and his associates to step aside to avert a military strike by the coalition force.

Rebels who had fought a bush war since 1991 have joined their cause with the coup soldiers, who accused ousted President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah of not working for national peace. Hundreds of rebels have entered the city since the coup on May 25.

Hundreds of foreigners taking refuge at the Mammy Yoko hotel under the protection of Nigerian troops were evacuated to basement shelters on Sunday night when three armed rebels entered the premises. They later left without an incident.
